newsitem.title: USA: American General forms two life divisions.
newsitem.headline: American General forms two life divisions.

text.p: American General Corp said on Wednesday it has created two divisions for its life insurance operations following the completion of its $1.8 billion acquisition of USLIFE Corp.
One division includes all life insurance operations that market life insurance and annuities through independent producers and general agents, American General said.
The other division is focused on the company's career agency distribution system, the company said.
The independent producer and general agent division will be comprised of American General Life, based in Houston and Franklin Life based in Springfield, Ill.

It also will include the recently acquired life insurance subsidiaries of USLIFE, including: United States Life Insurance Co based in New York City; Old Line Life based in Milwaukee; and All American Life based in Chicago.
The division will have a sales and distribution network of more than 18,000 agents.

The career agency division, which consists of American General Life and Accident Insurance Co based in Nashville, also includes two recently acquired life insurance companies -- Independent Life and Home Beneficial Life, American General said.
Both companies currently are being consolidated into American General Life and Accident.
Upon completion of this consolidation, the division will have over 7,000 career agents.

Rodney O. Martin, Jr., currently president and chief executive officer of American General Life, has been named to the additional post of president of the independent producer and general agent division, the company said.

He will be joined by two recently named division executive vice presidents: Christopher S. Ruisi, who served as president and chief operating officer of USLIFE Corp prior to the acquisition; and Carl J. Santillo, who has served as senior vice president - finance for American General Corp since 1996.
Joe Kelley, president and chief executive officer and Bill B. Luther, vice chairman of American General Life and Accident, will be responsible for the career agency division.

"The formation of this new divisional structure provides a solid foundation for ensuring the successful integration of USLIFE and the realization of significant operating efficiencies for American General's life insurance organization," American General chief executive Robert Devlin said.
The independent producer and general agent division will include centralized support units focused on product development, insurance administration, and operations support, the company said.
These support units will enable the division to leverage its newly expanded distribution system and product portfolio to benefit the entire group of companies, the company said.
The benefits of this centralized structure include improved product development and distribution, enhanced customer service, and a reduction in operating expenses, the company said.
